# Independent review of Python 3.10 test cleanup

Accepted the test-only successor `57fb1e80af400f4b7cfdb0fbac5bae34001f1b9a` over `7e997f794a92a0e517b7ad7ce3ee7fd862145a99`. Only the first statement in `InspectionTests.receive`'s finally block changes, with its explanatory comment. The strict callback, complete guarded try body, trace cleanup, post-inspection assertions and product source are unchanged.

The actual old CI job 113422504283 checked out the PR5 merge containing head `5478d8789503d518f7f24a23823a1872d3b4f7fa` with CPython 3.10.22. All 22 reported errors occur at the post-inspection `iterdump`. Its independently fetched log matches immutable blob `4686eec76b9cde03e8115ad915e8a0453c34f70f`.

[Official Python 3.11 documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/sqlite3.html#sqlite3.Connection.set_authorizer) dates None-disable support to 3.11. The exact [CPython 3.10.22 source](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.10.22/Modules/_sqlite/connection.c) passes None to the callback and maps the resulting call error to SQLITE_DENY. A callable returning SQLITE_OK is valid cleanup on that earlier contract.

The independent driver makes **42 focused checks**, without running the old suite. The modeled 3.10 baseline fails after its completed guarded SELECT; the local native 3.12 baseline passes. The candidate passes six helper calls in each mode, including repeated reads, native transitions, a typed missing-project refusal, an unexpected exception after the real SELECT, and an injected UPDATE. The UPDATE remains denied while inspection runs. All authorization callbacks during inspection are the original strict callback, and cleanup installation occurs only after inspection exits. A later native record_plan and repeated receiving succeed. All 15 original physical source files remain unchanged.

The model reproduces the inspected older callback outcome using local native SQLite; it is not an actual Python 3.10 run. Corrected hosted Python 3.10 CI remains the integration gate. All databases are authored :memory: fixtures; no filesystem output or operational route is exercised.

The initial reviewer driver had a reporting-footer brace SyntaxError before execution. Its exact output and reconstruction patch are retained; no product change resulted. The accepted driver and JSON argument are historical experiment inputs, not a new product command.

Author qualification remains in immutable receipt `f47caf6b0964cd4f5e0e27c0e4c533f3a5302ba0`; its memory-only driver and patch are not duplicated here.
